name: LIDAR-Lite v4 LED
description: Garmin's 10 m optical ranger using a 940 nm LED (no laser), I2C at 3.3 V logic, >200 Hz. Has an on-board nRF52840 you can reprogram, plus ANT wireless. Good for indoor robots that need eye-safe ranging.

variants.note: Garmin PN 010-02022-00. 2x5 through-holes, 2 mm pitch: VIN (5 V), GND, SDA, SCL, GPIOA, GPIOB, plus nRF52840 debug (VRETURN, nRESET, SWCLK, SWDIO). SparkFun SEN-15776, RobotShop RB-Pli-24.

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: LED emitter, not a laser. Garmin's manual gives no laser class; SparkFun describes the 940 nm LED as Class 1
Signal pins are 3.3 V max (5 V on SDA/SCL damages it) even though VIN needs 4.75-5.25 V. Internal 13 kΩ pull-ups, I2C address 0x62, 400 kHz
Update rate: >200 Hz typical over I2C, up to 200 Hz over ANT; Garmin states no default rate. Accuracy figures are 1σ repeatability in high-accuracy mode on a 90% target
Also does ANT wireless and can be set up for SPI with custom nRF52840 firmware (Nordic SDK); only I2C is listed here
2 mA idle, 85 mA during an acquisition. SparkFun sells a Qwiic version (SEN-18009) that runs from 3.3 V

specs.accuracy: ±1 cm to 2 m, ±2 cm to 4 m, ±5 cm to 10 m (1σ repeatability)
